title: Clinical manifestations and outcome in Staphylococcus aureus endocarditis among injection drug users and nonaddicts: a prospective study of 74 patients

claims.text: Endocarditis complicates 11% to 35% of S. aureus bacteremias (SAB), the range depending on the diagnostic criteria used.
claims.byte_quote: Endocarditis has been observed in 11% to 35% of S. aureus bacteremias (SAB)

claims.text: Among SAB cases, endocarditis was far more common in injection drug abusers (46%) than in nonaddicts (14%).
claims.byte_quote: Endocarditis was more common in SAB among drug abusers (46%) than in nonaddicts (14%)

claims.text: Injection drug abuse is one driver of the increased incidence of S. aureus infective endocarditis (host/exposure risk factor raising S. aureus).
claims.byte_quote: One of the reasons for increased incidence of S. aureus in IE is injection drug abuse

claims.text: Host factors raising endocarditis risk include S. aureus colonization, HIV-related immunosuppression, female sex, higher injection-drug-use frequency, and prior endocarditis.
claims.byte_quote: Colonization with S. aureus , HIV-related immunosuppression, female sex, increasing injection drug use frequency, and a history of previous IE are associated with a higher risk for endocarditis

claims.text: Injection drug users with S. aureus endocarditis were significantly younger than nonaddicts (mean 27 vs 65 years).
claims.byte_quote: IDUs were significantly younger (27 ± 15 vs 65 ± 15 years, P < 0.001)

claims.text: SAB in injection drug users was much more often community-acquired than in nonaddicts (95% vs 39%).
claims.byte_quote: their SAB was more often community-acquired (95% vs 39%, P < 0.001)

claims.text: Emerging at-risk host groups for S. aureus endocarditis are injection drug users, elderly patients with degenerative valve disease, patients with intravascular catheters or prosthetic valves, and nosocomial acquisition (device/exposure risk factors).
claims.byte_quote: new groups, including injection drug users (IDUs), elderly patients with degenerative valve disease, patients with intravascular catheter or prosthetic valve, and nosocomial acquisition

claims.text: Injection drug use predicts right-sided (tricuspid) endocarditis (60% of IDUs), whereas nonaddicts overwhelmingly have left-sided involvement (93%) — a portal/host-to-site association.
claims.byte_quote: Right-sided endocarditis was observed in 60% of IDUs whereas 93% of nonaddicts had left-sided involvement

claims.text: First-line antibiotic dosing for S. aureus endocarditis: cloxacillin or dicloxacillin 2 g IV every 4 hours for 4 to 6 weeks.
claims.byte_quote: All patients with endocarditis were assigned to receive initially cloxacillin or dicloxacillin (2 g q4 h) for 4 to 6 weeks intravenously

claims.text: Contraindication/alternative regimen: if semisynthetic penicillins are contraindicated, give cefuroxime 1.5 g every 6 h or vancomycin 1 g twice daily.
claims.byte_quote: Alternatively, cefuroxime (1.5 g q6 h) or vancomycin (1 g bid) were allowed if a contraindication against the use of semisynthetic penicillins was noted

claims.text: Adjunctive aminoglycoside dosing: tobramycin or netilmicin 1 mg/kg every 8 h added for the first 7 days.
claims.byte_quote: Aminoglycoside (either tobramycin or netilmicin at 1 mg/kg of body weight q8h) was added to the drug therapy described above for the first 7 days

claims.text: Adjunctive rifampicin dosing: 450 mg once daily if under 50 kg, 600 mg once daily if over 50 kg, oral or IV, for at least 4 weeks when endocarditis or extracardiac deep infection is suspected/confirmed (weight-banded dosing).
claims.byte_quote: Rifampicin (450 mg once daily for patients under 50 kg and 600 mg once daily for patients over 50 kg in weight, orally or intravenously) was recommended for at least 4 weeks

claims.text: In the actual cohort, 88% (65 of 74 patients) were treated with cloxacillin or dicloxacillin.
claims.byte_quote: Sixty-five of 74 patients (88%) were treated with cloxacillin or dicloxacillin
